newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet in jt bid for SNCF contract-Pascale.
newsitem.headline: Stet in jt bid for SNCF contract-Pascale.

text.p: Italy's Stet, Frances Bouygues and Germany's Veba will bid jointly next week to run the telephone infrastructure of French railway group SNCF, Stet Managing Director Ernesto Pascale said in an interview on Friday.

"On Monday Bouygues will present, together with the Germans at Veba, the joint offer to the French railways to become the strategic partner that they are looking for to develop and disseminate telecommunications services," said Pascale.
Pascale made the remarks in an interview with Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.
Bouygues announced on Thursday that Stet would take a 49 percent stake in a new company called Bouygues-Stet in which the French group would hold 51 percent.
The new company aims to become a big player in the French telecoms maarket after it is liberalised in 1998.
Pascale said Stet intended to collaborate with Bouygues in the full range of telecommunications services.

"We will start from mobile telephony, for which Bouygues has a licence to become the third French operator, but we are aiming to develop collaboration across the whole range of telecommunications services, including fixed line telephony," Pascale added.
Pascale said there could be scope for the two companies to turn their attention beyond France's borders.

"For the time being we foresee working together in France but it is evident that if opportunities for joint action with Bouygues arise even on an international level we will be very willing to seize them," said Pascale.
Pascale said the venture with Bouygues would enhance the global ambitions of Stet, which the Italian goverment has said it wants to privatise next year.

"It will make concrete our ambitions to operate across the board internationally with an eye above all on those markets and those businesses, such as those for big users, which are the most profitable," he added. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
